subject: POC observability & success criteria — proposed plan and timelines
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Cloud <ava@avacloud.io>, Diego Rojas <diego@avacloud.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: Discovery + POC goals (observability focus)

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off the POC next week.

Key goals you shared:
- Validate latency and tail behavior for user-facing prompt flows (target: p50 < 200ms, p95 < 550ms for 512-token requests)
- Measure cost per generated token under realistic traffic patterns and caching benefits
- Ensure traceability for hallucination investigations (request -> model variant -> prompt + KV cache snapshot)
- Confirm ability to export request logs and traces for your analytics stack (S3 + Datadog)

Proposed success criteria (please confirm or adjust):
1) Latency: p50/p95 targets met across 3 simulated scenarios (interactive, batch, high-concurrency).
2) Stability: <1% 5xx error rate and graceful fallback to a cheaper model variant under load.
3) Observability: end-to-end traces for 100% of sampled requests (trace IDs present in logs, exported to your Datadog account).
4) Cost: >=20% reduction vs your current baseline when using prefix caching + batching.
5) Data controls: logs exported to your S3 bucket with retention TTL you specify.

Operational ask from Ava Cloud (needed to start):
- A technical contact who can approve temporary IAM role for S3 export and Datadog API key;
- Expected test traffic profile (concurrency, request size distribution) by Friday;
- Any data residency/egress constraints.

I'll attach a short observability runbook and success criteria spreadsheet. Monica will lead CS coordination; Rishi will own the technical setup and perf tuning. Proposed timeline: 2-week setup + 2-week evaluation (4 weeks total).

Next steps: please confirm success criteria and share the technical contact and test profile.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: ava-poc-success-criteria.xlsx, observability-runbook.pdf

From: Diego Rojas <diego@avacloud.io>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ava Cloud <ava@avacloud.io>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Recap: Discovery + POC goals (observability focus)

Laura — thanks for the thorough recap. High level: all looks good. Quick answers and clarifications below.

Technical contact: Ava (CTO) and I will be primary contacts; she can approve the IAM role.
Test traffic profile (baseline we can share):
- Interactive: 40 RPS, average prompt 350 tokens, peak 120 RPS for 10 minutes;
- Batch: nightly bulk scoring ~10k requests at low priority;
- Concurrency target for stress test: 300 concurrent requests sustained for 5 minutes.

Data residency: US-only, no obvious egress blocks but our security team needs the runbook and network egress details.

Observability requirements:
- Trace sampling: 10% default + 100% for error cases;
- Structured logs: JSON with trace_id, request_id, user_id, model_variant;
- Export: S3 (logs) + Datadog (metrics/traces).

We reviewed the proposed p50/p95 numbers; we want to be pragmatic — if the initial numbers miss by a little, include an improvement plan and owner.

I'll attach our network egress requirements and will circulate to security.

— Diego
Diego Rojas
Engineering Lead, Ava Cloud
diego@avacloud.io

Attachments: network-egress-requirements.txt

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Rojas <diego@avacloud.io>, Ava Cloud <ava@avacloud.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: Discovery + POC goals (observability focus)

Thanks Diego — perfect, this gives us what we need to scope the network and security tasks. A few follow-ups and assignments from our side to keep things moving: 

Ownership (Redwood):
- Monica Patel (CS) — POC schedule, test-plan coordination, access approvals (monica.patel@redwood.ai)
- Rishi Malhotra (Solutions Eng) — workload generation, perf tuning, observability dashboard builds (rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai)

Observability plan (high-level):
1) Metrics to publish to Datadog (per-route and per-model): request_rate, tokens_generated, p50_latency, p95_latency, error_rate(4xx/5xx), kv_cache_hit_rate, model_fallback_count.
2) Tracing: propagate trace_id across client -> Redwood -> model runtime; include model_variant and kv_cache_snapshot_id as trace tags.
3) Logs: structured JSON + write to S3 prefixed by date/tenant (we'll use your bucket prefix if provided).
4) Dashboards: interactive dashboard template (we'll provision in your Datadog account) with top cards: latency histogram, error waterfall by model variant, cost per 1k tokens, cache-hit breakdown.
5) Alerts: p95_latency > 700ms for 5m; error_rate > 2% for 3m; model_fallback_count spike > 10/min.

Evaluation plan (how we'll judge success):
- Week 1 (setup): IAM role + keys, export path to S3, Datadog integration, baseline run of your traffic profile.
- Week 2 (tuning): run stress scenarios, iterate on batching/quantization profiles, enable prefix caching.
- Week 3–4 (evaluation): steady-state runs + user-simulated tests; collect metrics and traces for analysis against success criteria.

Deliverables at end of POC:
- Observability report (dashboards + selected traces)
- Cost delta analysis vs your baseline
- Runbook for production roll (recommended configs and autoscaling knobs)

I've attached a short observability runbook and a spreadsheet with measurable success criteria. Rishi will reach out with the synthetic workload generator and a first pass Datadog dashboard by Monday.

Can you confirm: preferred S3 prefix and a contact for Datadog API key exchange? Also, any corporate blackout windows next two weeks for maintenance?

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
